title: Nixtamalization at La Corona: Microbotanical analysis of ceramic vessels indicates Late Classic Maya cooking techniques
version: Quaternary International 711, pp. 38–48; DOI 10.1016/j.quaint.2024.09.007; first page from author-uploaded article and publisher section previews
lineage: Original analysis of a separate assemblage at La Corona by an independent team; uses the same published experimental diagnostic as San Bartolo. Publisher and author-hosted pages are versions of one paper. Full sample-level chronology and controls were unavailable.

passages.locator: Abstract, p. 38, and publisher’s Conclusion preview
passages.note: Spherulites detected in residues associated with food preparation or consumption, including burial and feasting contexts. Arguments are scoped to the seventh and eighth centuries at La Corona.
